**Finding submitted: deviation (high severity, ASSIGN).**

**What I found:** Section 15 (paragraph p0080, sitting in the run-on general-provisions block under the § 12 heading) is the only assignment provision in the Agreement. A full-text search confirms there is no "change of control" language anywhere — so, favorably for us, TrueLink has no change-of-control termination or re-pricing right, and I did not manufacture an issue there.

**Why it fails the fallback:**
- Client's only carve-out is an assignment to a "financially responsible affiliate" — there is **no successor / merger / sale-of-assets carve-out**, which is the core protection the rule exists to secure and which puts the clause at the edge of walk-away territory.
- The consent requirement binding Client is **unqualified** — no "not to be unreasonably withheld" standard, so the fallback's consent standard is also unmet.

**Redline (validated ok:true):** added the affiliate *and* merger/successor carve-out for Client, a reasonable-consent standard, a bar on TrueLink assigning to a Client competitor, and express confirmation that a Client change of control is neither an assignment nor a trigger for TrueLink termination, suspension or re-pricing. The comment offers the mutual notice-based fallback if TrueLink pushes back on the asymmetry.
